subject: Biotechnology
title: Tumor Mutational Burden
description: Learn Tumor Mutational Burden in one minute.

hook.text: More mutations mean more targets for the immune system — tumor mutational burden predicts immunotherapy response.

buildup.text: TMB counts mutations per megabase of DNA — high-TMB tumors create many neoantigens that T cells can recognize.

discovery.text: The FDA approved pembrolizumab for any high-TMB solid tumor — treatment based on genetics, not cancer type.

twist.text: TMB is not a perfect predictor — some high-TMB tumors do not respond, and some low-TMB tumors do.

climax.text: Combining TMB with PD-L1 expression and immune cell infiltration improves prediction — multi-biomarker panels emerge.

punchline.text: Count the mutations, predict the response — TMB guides immunotherapy decisions.

quiz.question: Why do high-TMB tumors respond better to immunotherapy?
options: High-TMB tumors grow more slowly, giving the immune system more time
More mutations create more neoantigens that immune cells can recognize and target
High-TMB tumors lack the ability to suppress immune responses

details.summary: Tumor mutational burden measures the total number of mutations per megabase of tumor DNA, serving as a biomarker for immunotherapy response. Tumors with high TMB generate more neoantigens that the immune system can recognize, making checkpoint inhibitor therapy more effective.
details.whyItMatters: TMB provides a tissue-agnostic biomarker for immunotherapy selection. The FDA approved pembrolizumab for any solid tumor with high TMB, regardless of cancer type.
takeaways: TMB above 10 mutations per megabase predicts better immunotherapy response
High TMB tumors generate more targets for immune recognition via neoantigens
FDA approved pembrolizumab for any TMB-high solid tumor regardless of type

faq.question: Why do highly mutated tumors respond better to immunotherapy?
faq.answer: More mutations create more abnormal proteins displayed on the tumor surface as neoantigens. The immune system can distinguish these abnormal proteins from normal self. Checkpoint inhibitors release the brake on T cells, which then recognize and attack cells displaying these abundant neoantigens.

faq.question: How is tumor mutational burden measured in clinical practice?
faq.answer: Targeted gene panels like FoundationOne CDx sequence about 1 megabase of coding genome and extrapolate total mutation rate. Whole exome sequencing provides more comprehensive measurement but is costlier. Harmonization of TMB measurement across platforms and labs remains an ongoing challenge.
